text: The internal logic of an arbitrary elementary topos is always classical, so the law of excluded middle holds in every topos.
explanation: False: the chapter stresses that a general topos has intuitionistic internal logic in which excluded middle may fail; only Boolean toposes (such as $\mathbf{Set}$ or $G\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$) are classical. Sheaf toposes $\mathrm{Sh}(X)$ are the standard counterexamples, with open sets serving as truth values.
